metadata.title: Claude, Contract Review.
metadata.subtitle: The Checklist, Not the Lawyer
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does a contract-review skill act like a lawyer, weighing judgment on your contract? Lands the carry-out that a SKILL.md gives Claude the same checklist every time — consistency, not judgment — so the read-through is still yours.
metadata.anchor_pair: NB06 -> NB08 (the same freelance contract, run twice, same termination flag)
metadata.one_flag: N/A - direct mechanism description throughout (see SCRIPT.md register audit)

beats.narration_text: People type it like this: is Claude my contract's lawyer? It isn't. It's my contract's checklist — the same steps, every single time. So what does that checklist actually catch, and what does it miss?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Is Claude my contract's lawyer?', hesitates on 'lawyer', corrects to 'checklist', lands the real question

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('lawyer' -> 'checklist') lands on screen.

beats.narration_text: People hand Claude a contract expecting a review. What actually runs in between is a written file: SKILL.md.

shot.new_visual_element: Contract in, SKILL.md, then the mechanism

production_viz.label: A contract goes in
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips connected by arrows: YOUR CONTRACT, SKILL.md, ??? (accented) — the unknown is what happens in between.

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption: Claude reads it like a lawyer would, weighing the whole document clause by clause, case by case.

shot.new_visual_element: The lawyer's-judgment reading, sold as reasonable

production_viz.label: The natural guess
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips connected by arrows: READ IT ALL, WEIGH EACH CLAUSE, LAWYER'S CALL (accented) — the wrong guess, stated fairly.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. SKILL.md is the whole instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic.

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips, no arrows: SKILL.md, PLAIN LANGUAGE, NO HIDDEN LOGIC.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline is fixed: read the file, execute each step in order, return the result. Linear — no branching unless a step says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Read, execute, return — the fixed pipeline

production_viz.label: The pipeline is fixed
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips connected by arrows: READ STEPS, EXECUTE IN ORDER, RETURN RESULT.

beats.narration_text: So it isn't judgment — it's a checklist, written in advance. That trade buys repeatable results: the same input gets the same output, every run.

production_viz.label: Checklist, not judgment
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips, no arrows, accent on the third: CHECKLIST, NOT JUDGMENT, REPEATABLE (accented).

beats.narration_text: Run it on a freelance contract, and it flags the termination clause. The checklist says look there, so it looks.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — freelance contract, termination clause flagged

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a freelance contract
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Three chips connected by arrows, accent on the third: FREELANCE CONTRACT, TERMINATION CLAUSE, FLAGGED (accented). THIS EXACT CHIP ('FREELANCE CONTRACT') RETURNS AT NB08.

beats.narration_text: But the checklist only names what it names. An arbitration clause the list never mentions gets no comment — not because it's fine.

production_viz.label: Off the list, no comment
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips connected by arrows, accent on the second: ON THE LIST, OFF THE LIST (accented), NO COMMENT.

beats.narration_text: Run the same contract again: the termination flag comes back, identical. That's consistency — a flag means a listed check matched, not a verdict on the contract.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same contract, same flag, not a verdict

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same flag
production_viz.mechanic: THE NB06 CHIP RETURNS. Three chips connected by arrows, accent on the third: FREELANCE CONTRACT, SAME FLAG, NOT A VERDICT (accented).

beats.narration_text: And a clean pass isn't a clean bill of health either — it means nothing on the list tripped. What's off the list stays invisible either way.

shot.new_visual_element: A clean pass isn't a clean bill of health

production_viz.label: A clean pass isn't safety
production_viz.mechanic: Three chips connected by arrows, accent on the third: CLEAN PASS, NOTHING TRIPPED, STILL INVISIBLE (accented).

beats.narration_text: A SKILL.md gives Claude the same checklist every time — that's consistency, not judgment, so the read-through is still yours.

props.quote: A SKILL.md gives Claude the same checklist every time — that's consistency, not judgment, so the read-through is still yours.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, along with any contract you're reviewing: 'Before you review this, list exactly what you will check for and what you will not. Then do the review.' That first list turns an invisible checklist into one you can see.

props.command: Before you review this contract, list exactly what you will check for and what you will not. Then do the review.

beats.narration_text: Claude, Contract Review — the checklist, not the lawyer. Liam, in for Bear.
